title: Reuters reportedly: hackers breached the US Air Force's Cloud One platform, attackers and scope unknown
date_note: The pages give only their own publication day, 27 November; they say the breach was discovered about a month earlier during a system update.
geo_basis: country: the platform belongs to the US Air Force, no city is stated
summary: Euronews Arabic, Annahar and Bankingnews, all relaying Reuters and anonymous sources, report that hackers breached the Air Force's Cloud One platform. One source told Reuters the attackers exploited a software vulnerability to reach the control plane. Migrations and updates were halted and some users' administrator privileges revoked. Who is behind it, the full scope and whether data was stolen are not known.
plain: Reuters, as relayed by three outlets, reports that hackers got into the US Air Force's main cloud platform. Some work on it was suspended. Who did it and whether data was taken is not known.
exec: Reuters, via three outlets, reports a breach of an Air Force cloud platform that disrupted migrations and updates; scope and attacker are unknown.

validation.note: Bankingnews, Euronews Arabic and Annahar all relay one Reuters report based on anonymous sources; the Reuters original was not found or read, and no official statement was read.
